source.title: HW-GPT-Bench: Hardware-Aware Architecture Benchmark for Language Models
source.authors: R. Sukthanker; Arber Zela; B. Staffler; Aaron Klein; L. Purucker; J. Franke; Frank Hutter

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how architectural choices relate to perplexity in GPT-2-family subnetworks, but does not test parameter/token/compute scaling laws, extrapolation, or perplexity at fixed parameter count. Its architecture results therefore do not test any listed claim version as stated.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fitted relationships between architectural dimensions and perplexity. These are relevant to architecture/perplexity but are not results at fixed parameter count, and do not test the listed scaling-law versions. Hardware-surrogate and NAS results concern different outcomes and are not claim-relevant rows.
record.test_reason: This is a hardware-aware NAS benchmark. It cites Hoffmann et al. only as background. Its power-law fits relate perplexity to architecture dimensions (layers, embedding dim, MLP ratio, heads, bias) across 10k subnetworks. Those subnetworks inherit weights from a weight-sharing supernet; none is trained independently. Parameter count is not held fixed, so the fits cannot test V4. Parameters, tokens and compute are not varied as scaling axes, so V1–V3 are not tested either. No other version is addressed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present HW-GPT-Bench as a surrogate benchmark for hardware-aware multi-objective NAS. They report AutoGluon surrogates as accurate and calibrated, and that embedding dimension matters most for perplexity in their spaces.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates architecture/perplexity associations in weight-sharing GPT-2 supernetworks; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted architecture-to-perplexity coefficients differ across GPT-S, GPT-M, GPT-L and the wide search spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: In supernet-inherited GPT-2 subnetworks, fitted architecture-to-perplexity exponents put embedding dimension as most influential (e exponent about -0.31 to -0.38). The layer-count exponent shrinks from GPT-S to GPT-L (-0.226 to -0.073).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within weight-sharing GPT-2 search spaces, perplexity depends most on embedding dimension, and the relative weight of depth falls at larger supernet scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Kendall-tau between params and 1/perplexity is about 0.92 (GPT-S), 0.86 (GPT-M) and 0.85 (GPT-L) across 10k inherited subnetworks (Figs 62-64).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter count rank-predicts inherited-subnetwork perplexity within a supernet; this is a monotone association, not a power-law loss scaling result.

record.problems: The architecture/perplexity analysis does not compare architectures at fixed parameter count. The reported perplexities come from inherited weights in a weight-sharing supernetwork rather than independently trained models.

untested.parts: Loss vs parameters, tokens or compute for independently trained models; the paper reports only rank correlations of 1/perplexity with params inside a supernet.
Extrapolation from small to large runs.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count; the architecture fits do not hold parameters fixed.
Downstream predictability; accuracy is next-token accuracy only, correlated with perplexity.
Dependence of scaling exponents or the compute-optimal split on setup choices.

record.verdict_notes: The power-law form here is assumed 'for analysis purposes' over architecture choices. It is not a scaling law in N, D or C. All perplexities come from weights inherited from a sandwich-trained supernet, not from independently trained models. Inherited perplexity correlates with perplexity after fine-tuning (Kendall-tau 0.93-0.96, Table 11).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss scaling in parameter count, training tokens, and compute.
Predicting much larger runs from fits on smaller runs.
Comparisons at a fixed parameter count; the reported architecture variations do not hold parameter count fixed.
Dependence of the cited scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: GPT-S
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power-law relationship between architectural dimensions and inherited-subnetwork perplexity.
rows.measure: Fitted perplexity relationship to layers, embedding dimension, MLP ratio, heads, and bias
rows.note: The authors describe embedding dimension as the most important architecture parameter. This is not a fixed-parameter-count comparison.
rows.check: Fit of perplexity against architecture dimensions, not against parameters, data or compute. Parameter count varies with the dimensions, and weights are inherited from a supernet. 'observed' has no version to attach to, so cannot_determine.
